motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve the Consent Agenda with changes to Item 16.A. as discussed in Work Session . Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Routine consent items approved in one vote
motions.summary: The council approved its consent agenda, a batch of routine items passed together, with a change to one item worked out earlier in the work session.
motions.impact: This is routine housekeeping — nothing here changes for residents. The minutes do not list which items were in the batch.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Accepting the Eagle Mountain City Tentative Budget for Fiscal Year 2026 -2027 and Setting a Public Hearing for the Interim Budget on for June 16, 2026 and Setting a Public Hearing for Budget Adoption o n August 18, 2026.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Accepting the Eagle Mountain Tentative Budget for Fiscal Year 2026 —2027 and Setting a Public Hearing for the Interim Budget on for June 16, 2026 and Setting a Public Hearing for Budget Adoption on August 18, 2026. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Draft 2026-27 budget accepted, hearings scheduled
motions.summary: The council accepted the city's tentative budget for fiscal year 2026-2027 and set public hearings for June 16 and August 18, 2026.
motions.impact: Nothing changes day to day — this is the routine first step in the budget process. If you want a say in next year's spending, those two hearing dates are your chance.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Acknowledging the Budget Officer’s Statement of a Proposed Property Tax Increase and Property Tax Impact Schedule (Truth -in-Taxation Compliance).
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Acknowledging the Budget Officers Statement of a Proposed Property Tax Increase and Property Tax Impact Schedule (Truth-in-Taxation Compliance). Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: City logs the figures behind a possible tax increase
motions.summary: The council formally acknowledged the budget officer's statement of a proposed property tax increase and the schedule showing what it would mean for property owners.
motions.impact: This is a required paperwork step in the tax increase process — nothing changes for you yet. The decision on whether to actually raise the rate comes later.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Declaring Intent to Increase Property Tax Revenue, Providing Notice, and Setting a Public Hearing Date in Accordance with Truth -in-Taxation Requirements.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to approve a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Declaring Intent to Increase Property Tax Revenue, Providing Notice, and Setting a Public Hearing Date in Accordance with the Truth -in-Taxation Requirements. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Notice given of a proposed property tax increase
motions.summary: The council took up a resolution declaring the city's intent to raise property tax revenue and setting the public hearing required before any increase can happen.
motions.impact: Nothing changes yet — this is the notice step. Before the city can raise property taxes, it must hold a public hearing where residents can speak for or against it.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Parks, Trails, and Open Space Master Plan and Impact Fee Facilities Plan (IFFP) with an update to include Sweetwater Park cost in the IFFP
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Parks, Trails, and Open Space Master Plan and Impact Fee Facilities Plan (IFFP) with an update to include Sweetwater Park cost in the IFFP. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Parks plan adopted, Sweetwater Park cost added
motions.summary: The council adopted the parks, trails, and open space master plan and added the cost of Sweetwater Park to the list of projects impact fees are meant to fund.
motions.impact: This is the roadmap for future parks and trails and the project list that fees on new homes help pay for. Nothing gets built yet and nothing changes on your bill today.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Official Zoning Map and Future Land Use Map to Assign Current Zoning Designations to the Brandon Park Area as presented
motions.motion: Councilmember Whiting moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Official Zoning Map and Future Land Use Map to Assign Current Zoning Designations to the Brandon Park Area as presented . Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Zoning map updated for the Brandon Park area
motions.summary: The city formally recorded existing zoning designations for the Brandon Park area on its official zoning map and future land use map.
motions.impact: This is a bookkeeping fix that puts zoning already in use onto the official maps. If you own property in Brandon Park, your designation is now clearly on the record.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.72 regarding Commercial and Multifamily Design Standards as presented . Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion. Eagle Mountain City CouMnicnilu te –s May 52, 026 Page1 0 of 14
motions.headline: Design standards updated for shops and apartments
motions.summary: The council adopted changes to the city's design standards for commercial and apartment buildings, approving them as presented without detailing them in the motion.
motions.impact: These rules apply to future commercial and apartment projects, so builders deal with them directly, not current homeowners. The minutes do not say what specifically changed.

motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.55 Off-Street Parking and 17.60 Landscaping, Buffering, Fencing and Transitioning with the following updates: 1. Use the Planning Commission Recommendation; and 2. All sides where screening is required for a residential element be 3 ½ feet at time of planting and work with staff on proper placement of the monument sign so it is not shielded; and 3. Require v egetation used to provide year -round screening. Councilmember Whiting seconded the motion.
motions.headline: New screening rules between homes and parking lots
motions.summary: The city rewrote its parking and landscaping rules, requiring plants that screen homes to be 3.5 feet tall when planted and to stay green year-round.
motions.impact: You would notice this on new commercial and apartment projects next to houses: thicker, evergreen screening from day one instead of thin or bare hedges. Developers carry the cost.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Spring Run Plaza Master Development Agreement.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, U tah, Approving the Spring Run Plaza Master Development Agreement with a change of language to read: 1. 4.3(d) N o more than 10 feet of landscap e width is required in any location ; and 2. 4.3(f) If approved by City Staff and City Council, retaining walls taller than 6 feet do not need to be tiered so long as the walls are designed and engineered to provide for structural integrity and geotechnical stability and prohibiting boulder or rock s tacked walls. Councilmember Huish seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Spring Run Plaza deal: less landscaping, taller walls
motions.summary: The council approved the development agreement for Spring Run Plaza, capping required landscaping at 10 feet wide and allowing engineered retaining walls over 6 feet without stepping them back.
motions.impact: This sets the rules the developer must follow. Neighbors may see a narrower planted buffer and taller, single-face retaining walls, though stacked boulder or rock walls are not allowed.

motions.item_title: Approve Preliminary Plat for Spring Run Plaza on a 27.35 acre parcel at the northeast corner of…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve Preliminary Plat for Spring Run Plaza on a 27.35 acre parcel at the northeast corner of Spring Run Parkway and Cory B. Wride Memorial Highway. Phase 1 (8.15 area) includes six lots, with Lots 7 and 8 remaining undeveloped with the understanding that when they are ready for development, the master development documents would be amended . Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Spring Run Plaza: 6 lots approved on 27-acre site
motions.summary: The city signed off on the first layout for Spring Run Plaza, a 27.35-acre commercial site at Spring Run Parkway and Cory B. Wride Memorial Highway.
motions.impact: If you live or drive near that corner, expect work to start on the first 8.15 acres. Two lots stay empty for now, and the city has to revisit the plans before those are built.
